subject.title: [Feature]: Batch WhatsApp messages by messageTimestamp instead of receive time

question: Should WhatsApp add opt-in platform-timestamp coalescing, and if so what timestamp tolerance, maximum hold, default state, and command/media flush semantics should become the public contract?
rationale: Source inspection establishes the behavioral gap, but code alone cannot choose the acceptable latency-versus-collision tradeoff or whether configuration belongs only to WhatsApp or to a shared inbound policy.

options.title: WhatsApp opt-in coalescing
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default WhatsApp setting with a narrow timestamp tolerance and hard maximum hold, preserving current behavior for existing users.

options.title: Shared channel coalescing
options.body: Design a cross-channel session-and-sender coalescer first, accepting broader architecture and configuration work before addressing WhatsApp.

options.title: Keep arrival-time debounce
options.body: Retain current semantics and document that users must raise debounceMs when Baileys delivery skew exceeds the configured window.

recommendation.title: WhatsApp opt-in coalescing
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default WhatsApp setting with a narrow timestamp tolerance and hard maximum hold, preserving current behavior for existing users.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing review plus shared debounce, configuration, and documentation history make this the strongest available routing candidate for the product-contract decision.
